limitations: No recording of this combination exists: all figure motions are DESIGNED to follow the reading the user approved (sketch); the puck follows from them through contacts, ice friction and the boards.

Left-wing pass (v2): soft reception, then a forward push into the corner, from the user's physics example (references/shots/lw-board-pass-example.mov, a different combination). The example's speeds were read with an uncalibrated scale (about 1 m/s along the end board); the trace releases at about 1.3 m/s because the preview ice friction (spjass fit, 926 mm/s^2) is higher than the example suggests.

Slide-or-bounce limits (500 mm/s figure impacts, 300 mm/s board/post impacts) are assumed by Claude from the user's rule; the frictionless e = 0.5 contact makes the push a series of small touches (each below 100 mm/s after the first).

CATCH POINT MOVED: in the sketch the right wing receives about 18 cm from the goal line. Along the board the puck is 37 mm from his slot, so only the board-side face of his blade can reach it and the shot can leave at most about 35-40 deg from the board; he receives it about 26 cm from the goal line.
Goalie pose assumed: E-G covers the left post (y = +20 mm, drawn there by the cross pass to the left wing).
Collision rule ASSUMED: blade/skate-puck restitution 0.5, frictionless; boards, posts and cage inelastic. Ice friction from the spjass slide fit.
Blade, skate and stick geometry are the AI-modelled mold at the assumed preview scale; puck thickness and goal size are preview values; the cage is modelled as its footprint (side and back nets).
